ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-1: Zero-price bypass in validateHandlerOrder — computeRatioX96 returns 0 on overflow, validateHandlerOrder does NOT check for sqrtPriceX96==0 (unlike _validatePricingBounds which does)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Missing zero check only affects CLOB order placement (not AMM swaps). Maker controls their own order price — bypassing max-only bounds lets maker place bad orders against themselves. Taker must accept to fill. No involuntary value extraction. Low/informational inconsistency.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-2: Direct handler call — calling CLOBTransferHandler directly (not via AMM) to bypass pricing enforcement
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOBTransferHandler.ammHandleTransfer checks msg.sender == AMM (line 230). afterSwapRefund also checks msg.sender == AMM (line 316). No executeSwap function exists. Handler ONLY accepts calls from AMM contract.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-3: Settings sync gap — hook settings cache in AMMStandardHook can desync from CreatorHookSettingsRegistry
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Desync is documented and by-design (CreatorHookSettingsRegistry.sol lines 24-53). Enables grandfathering, isolation, gradual rollout. Sync is explicit via hooksToSync parameter. Admin-controlled configuration, not attacker-exploitable.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-4: Transient storage leak — DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT may retain stale data between swaps
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: EIP-1153 clears transient storage per-transaction. Within a transaction, AMM calls beforeSwap then afterSwap atomically per swap — no interleaving. HOOK-001 overwrite (second token call overwrites first) is by-design. Direct swap pricing uses latest write.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H1: Flash loan → CLOB self-trade at extreme price → AMM reads distorted state
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: AMM reads price from pool type contract (getCurrentPriceX96), not from CLOB order book. CLOB prices are per-order-book and isolated from AMM pool pricing. No cross-venue price contamination path exists.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H2: snapPrice in addLiquidity allows arbitrary price movement → sandwich
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: DynamicHelper.snapPrice requires poolState.liquidity == 0 AND no initialized ticks between current and target. Cannot sandwich active pools. Zero-liquidity pools have nothing to extract.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H3: SingleProviderPoolType trusts external pricing hook → oracle spoof
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Hook is set by pool creator at pool creation time. Only the pool creator can set their pool's pricing hook. Malicious hook = self-inflicted config error (FP pattern #4). No external attacker can inject a hook into someone else's pool.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H4: Direct swap bypasses pricing bounds checked by hooks
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Direct swaps call beforeSwap AND afterSwap hooks. _validatePricingBounds has explicit direct swap path (poolType == address(0)) that stores input amount in transient storage (beforeSwap) then validates computed price from both amounts (afterSwap). Direct swap pricing IS enforced.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H5-H8: Oracle stale price / unbounded oracle / TWAP manipulation / front-run oracle update
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Limit Break AMM does not use external oracles (Chainlink, TWAP, etc.) for pricing. Pool types compute prices internally. No stale oracle, no TWAP, no oracle update to front-run.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H9: Controlled hook returns fake sqrtPriceX96
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Same as H3 — hook is set by pool/token creator. External attacker cannot inject hooks. Self-inflicted config.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H10: Bypass slippage/deadline params
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: AMM contract has no explicit slippage parameter. Slippage protection is caller-enforced (router pattern). No protocol-level slippage to bypass.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: PROBE-1: Dust-loop extraction via 100+ tiny swaps
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fee calculation uses mulDivRoundingUp — 1-wei inputs with 30bps fee pay ceil(30/10000) = 1 fee, consuming entire input. Zero output for all 100 iterations. Pool always gains from dust swaps.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: PROBE-2: Forged hook caller with fake pool identity
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All hook entry points (beforeSwap, afterSwap, validateAddLiquidity, validatePoolCreation) check msg.sender == AMM via _requireCallerIsAMM(). registryUpdate* functions check msg.sender == SETTINGS_REGISTRY. No external caller can fake hook interactions.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: PROBE-3: Transient-slot theft — write slot in path A, read stale in path B
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Transient storage is per-contract (EVM spec). Only AMMStandardHook can read/write its own transient slots. AMM calls before/afterSwap atomically per swap — no interleaving between different swaps' hook calls.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: PROBE-4: Permit mutation — replay with mutated unsigned feeOnTop field
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: feeOnTop is NOT signed in SWAP_TYPEHASH (documented, by-design). But feeOnTop only affects executor's service fee — it doesn't redirect victim funds. Victim's swap still executes at agreed permit terms. PermitC approval bounds total transfer amount.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: PROBE-5: Storage-slot collision across diamond proxy facets
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Architecture uses single implementation (AMMModule) with dedicated storage slot (0x9A1D). Pool types, handlers, and hooks are separate external contracts called via regular calls (not delegatecall). No multi-facet diamond with shared storage to collide.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: INV-SW02: No profitable round-trip (A→B→A)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge fuzz tests across all pool types confirm: output <= input after fees and rounding. mulDiv rounds down (output), mulDivRoundingUp rounds up (cost). Rounding always favors protocol. Tested at 25+ fuzz runs per pool type.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: INV-SW03: Rounding favors protocol (sequential 1-wei swaps)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: 1000+ sequential 1-wei swaps never decrease pool balance. Fee calculation with mulDivRoundingUp ensures minimum 1 wei fee on any non-zero input. 0.3% fee on 1 wei = ceil(0.003) = 1 → full input consumed as fee.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Lens-1: Fee value denomination mismatch (MUX-style bug)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fee is always computed and transferred in the same token denomination. No cross-token fee application. Unlike MUX, there's no point where a fee computed in token A is applied as token B.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Lens-3: Amplification factor in fee*amount or price*quantity
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All multiplications use FullMath.mulDiv with correct denominators. Fee rate (BPS) × amount uses MAX_BPS denominator. sqrtPriceX96 × amount uses Q96 denominator. feeGrowth × liquidity uses Q128 denominator. No denomination mismatch in any multiplication site.

theft_theses.thesis: Flash loan → CLOB self-trade at extreme price → AMM reads distorted state → extract on AMM
snapPrice allows arbitrary price movement → sandwich around snapPrice
SingleProviderPoolType trusts external pricing hook → oracle spoof
Direct swap bypasses pricing bounds → swap at distorted price
Controlled hook returns fake sqrtPriceX96 → attacker swaps at rigged price
Bypass slippage/deadline → execute swap at worse-than-expected price
validateHandlerOrder zero-price bypass allows CLOB order at extreme price
Permit feeOnTop mutation redirects victim funds
